Subject: SIG: access controls follow-up — least privilege + exception log

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the initial SIG intake earlier — Acme's procurement/security team is running the access controls slice now. We've got a couple of focused asks before we close the security review:

- A signed attestation that Redwood enforces least-privilege for production roles (short paragraph + signatory).
- A current RBAC matrix export showing role -> privilege mappings for production (redact user-specific PII).
- SCIM provisioning mapping for our tenant (which attributes are synced, how group-to-role mappings are handled).
- Your exception log for the last 12 months (approved deviations to least-privilege, with justification and compensating controls).

We prefer files in XLSX/CSV/PDF, and if any logs contain PII please send redacted versions. I've attached a nominal SIG worksheet with sections highlighted for access controls (SIG_questionnaire_v3.xlsx).

Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? If a signed attestation is easier via DocuSign we can accept that.

Thanks,
Elena

Thanks Ben. Quick notes for evidence team before we send anything externally:

- RBAC matrix: remove any full email addresses and user_ids; replace with role-owner aliases (e.g., ROLE_DB_ADMIN -> owner: db-team). Keep role descriptions and which scopes they grant.
- Exception log: include date opened/closed, approver, justification, and compensating controls. Strip incident identifiers that could expose customer info.
- SCIM mapping: include attribute list (username, email, givenName, familyName, groups) and a one-page summary of group->role rules. Detailed attribute-level mapping can be sanitized.
- MFA/SAML evidence: provide screenshots of SSO policy (showing MFA required for production apps) and a short note on our IdP enforcement (we use SAML federation + Okta/Google as IdP customers choose).
- Retention: confirm we redacted logs but retain timestamps for audit (90 days default; compliance may request longer).

I'm happy to review PDF artifacts before they go out. I'll also prepare a short readme that calls out what was redacted and why.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
